Not the derby night we wanted | Millwall U21 1-0 West Ham U21

13th October 2026
Mark Carlaw (@markcarlaw)

Fri 9 Oct 2026, The Den | U21 Premier League Cup, Group F

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:21
Instaread

Our Under-21s went down 1-0 at The Den, with Jack Howland’s 63rd-minute finish the difference. It ends a five-game unbeaten run for Mark Robson’s young Irons, and our wait for a first win in this season’s Premier League Cup goes on.

We started well. Within minutes Joel Kerr sprang a counter, Dan Cummings raced on and looked for Jethro Medine, but Millwall scrambled it clear.

Then came an early blow. Junior Robinson went off with a concussion on 26 minutes. Andre Dike came on and Jethro Medine moved to right-back.

Millwall grew into it. Josh Briggs and Ezra Mayers threw themselves in front of a Jaydon Thomas-Smith shot, and just before the break Howland curled a free-kick just wide of the near post. It was 0-0 at half-time.

Our best chance came just before the hour. Jethro Medine picked out his brother Jephthah with a pinpoint cross, but the volley flew over from inside the box.

Almost straight away, we were punished. Caleb Redhead teed up Howland, who slotted past Lanre Awesu into the bottom corner.

Awesu and Dike kept us in it after that. Awesu gathered one Thomas-Smith effort and blocked another one-on-one late on, and Dike tracked back brilliantly to stop Redhead getting a clear run at goal.

Then, with almost the last kick, Cummings met Riley Hargan’s corner unmarked at the back post and volleyed over. So close.

“I thought that we competed really well against a strong, physical side,” Robson said to the clubs Official Website. “Having said that, in possession, we just weren’t at the races tonight. We kept giving the ball away and getting caught on it because we were too slow.

“It’s an eye-opener for all the boys. It was a tough one for them and it was hard for the younger lads to adapt.”

He’s right. Millwall’s own stat line had them on 13 shots to our six. For a side that’s created plenty this season, this was a night where we never really got going.

One bright spot was 17-year-old Chuk Obi off the bench. “I thought he did really well when he came on,” Robson said. “He dealt very well with Millwall’s physicality.”

It’s one point from three games in Group F. Brighton beat Sheffield United 2-1 on the same night to stay top, and Millwall are up and running.

There are three group games left: Sheffield United at Rush Green on 30 October, Brighton away on 23 November and Millwall at home in December. We’ll probably need to win at least two of them.

Robson called it “a bit of a blip”, and there’s no time to dwell on it. We’re at Braintree Town tonight (Tue 13 Oct, 7:30pm) in the National League Cup. Then it’s Norwich away in PL2 on Friday, and Monaco II on 20 October.

The teams
Millwall U21: Przewozny; Beaumont, Ojetoro (Emuze HT), Mansour (c), Parkes (Taylor 59), Ofori-Manteaw, Howland (Anderson 69), Payton, Redhead (Ndige 85), Tsugita Vieira, Thomas-Smith.
Subs not used: Ndikum (GK), Snelgrove, Jacome.
Goal: Howland 63. Booked: Payton, Thomas-Smith.

West Ham U21: Awesu; Robinson (Dike 26), Mayers, Briggs (c), Leacock, Omotoye (Morris 57), Jethro Medine, Hargan, Cummings, Jephthah Medine (Obi 71), Kerr (Balogun 89).
Subs not used: Hooper (GK), Beckford, Montague.
